081: The line drawn halfway between the upper and lower surfaces of an aerofoil is the:
The straight line from the leading edge to the trailing edge is the:
Cuerda = recta. La curva equidistante es la línea de curvatura media.
The angle between the chord line and the relative airflow is the:
Ángulo de ataque = cuerda ↔ viento relativo. La incidencia es cuerda ↔ eje longitudinal.
At which point of an aerofoil do the upper and lower airflows rejoin?
The upper and lower airflows meet again
The airflow first makes contact with the aerofoil
The main spar of the wing is always located
The ribs end and the wingtip begins
En el borde de salida se juntan los flujos de extradós e intradós.
The intrados of an aerofoil is its:
The thickness of an aerofoil is:
The maximum distance between the upper and lower surfaces
The distance from the leading edge to the trailing edge
The distance between the mean camber line and the chord
The span divided by the chord
★ Pregunta típica. Lo de borde de ataque a borde de salida es la cuerda.
For a straight-tapered wing, the mean geometric chord is:
★ MGC = superficie / envergadura = (raíz + punta) / 2 en un ala trapezoidal. «Borde de ataque + borde de salida» era el error de los apuntes.
Viewed from the front, a wing whose tips are lower than its root has:
Puntas abajo = anhedral; puntas arriba = diedro.
Dihedral is NOT measured against the:
The longitudinal axis of the fuselage
The relative wind in level flight
The chord line of the wing root
El diedro se mide respecto al plano horizontal del avión (eje lateral).
The reference wing area includes the portion of the wing hidden inside the fuselage.
False: only the exposed area counts
False: it includes the tailplane instead
Trial: la parte tapada por el fuselaje cuenta.
When the pilot rolls right with the ailerons, adverse yaw tends to yaw the nose:
Left, because the up-going left wing has more induced drag
Right, because the right wing has more lift
Down, because the elevator is affected
Nowhere: ailerons act only about the longitudinal axis
Alabeo a la derecha → guiñada adversa a la izquierda.
With differential ailerons, which aileron moves through the larger angle?
Both move through the same angle
El que sube se mueve más: más resistencia en el ala que baja y menos guiñada adversa.
How does a Frise aileron reduce adverse yaw?
The up-going aileron's leading edge protrudes below the wing
The down-going aileron's leading edge protrudes above the wing
It moves the rudder automatically in the same direction
It is mounted at the leading edge, ahead of the spar
Frise: el borde de ataque del alerón que sube asoma por debajo y crea resistencia.
Deflecting the ailerons moves the rudder automatically to counter adverse yaw
Deflecting the rudder moves the elevator
The ailerons move only when the rudder is used
The ailerons and flaps always move together
Alabeas y el rudder se mueve solo para corregir la guiñada adversa.
Roll and yaw are said to be coupled because:
Rolling produces a yawing moment, and yawing a rolling one
Both are controlled by the same control surface
Both happen about the lateral axis of the aircraft
They are both controlled with the rudder pedals
★ Importante: alabeo y guiñada están acoplados.
Extending the flaps, the critical (stalling) angle of attack:
Flaps reduce the stall speed mainly because they increase:
★ Importante: suben el coeficiente de sustentación.
Increase the critical angle of attack
Decrease the critical angle of attack
Spoil the airflow over the upper surface
★ Importante: los slats aumentan el α crítico.
A higher outside air temperature (higher density altitude) has the following effect on the climb performance:
It reduces both the climb angle and the rate of climb
It increases the climb angle only
It increases the rate of climb but reduces the climb angle
It has no effect if the IAS is maintained
Más temperatura = aire menos denso: menos potencia y menos exceso de empuje/potencia, y la TAS para la misma IAS es mayor. Bajan ángulo y régimen de ascenso.
Compared with a cold day, on a hot day at the same pressure altitude the aeroplane's climb gradient will be:
Larger, but the rate of climb smaller
Con calor la densidad cae y el motor da menos potencia: gradiente y régimen de ascenso disminuyen.
Which of the following combinations gives the WORST climb performance?
High temperature, high altitude, high mass
Low temperature, low altitude, low mass
Low temperature, high altitude, low mass
High temperature, low altitude, low mass
Peor ascenso con calor + altitud + peso: densidad baja y mucha masa que subir.
When an aeroplane flies in ground effect (within about one wingspan of the surface), the aeroplane experiences:
A reduction in induced drag and an increase in lift for the same angle of attack
An increase in induced drag and a reduction in lift
An increase in the stall speed
A greater downwash at the tailplane and a nose-up pitching moment
Cerca del suelo los torbellinos de punta de ala se debilitan: baja el ángulo inducido, baja la resistencia inducida y, para el mismo ángulo de ataque, sube la sustentación (el avión «flota»).
Which of the following is NOT an effect of ground effect?
An increase in the induced drag
A reduction in the induced drag
A reduction in the stall speed
The aeroplane tends to float on the flare
Ground effect REDUCE la resistencia inducida; por eso el avión flota y la velocidad de pérdida baja ligeramente.
Ground effect is most noticeable at a height above the surface of approximately:
Only on the runway itself, never over grass
Se nota por debajo de una envergadura y es máximo a una fracción de ella.
In ground effect, the downwash at the tailplane is reduced. For a conventional tail this produces:
A yawing moment to the left
Menos downwash en la cola = mayor ángulo de ataque efectivo del estabilizador, más sustentación en la cola y tendencia a picar.
050: As air density decreases, density altitude:
Inversa: menos densidad, más altitud de densidad.
Which statement about density altitude is correct?
High DA means thin air and worse performance
High DA means dense air and better performance
DA does not depend on temperature at all
DA always equals true altitude in flight
DA alta = aire poco denso = peor.
Density altitude is best described as:
True altitude corrected for the wind
The altitude read with QFE set
The altitude read with QNH set
DA es la PA corregida por temperatura no estándar.
An airfield's density altitude is much higher than its elevation. The air is:
Less dense than ISA: worse performance
DA por encima de la elevación = aire menos denso.
Same aerodrome on two days: QNH 1030 and QNH 1000. Performance is better with:
Both, pressure altitude is the same
Más presión = PA más baja = mejor.
On a standard (ISA) day, pressure altitude equals:
En el raro día estándar, PA = altitud verdadera.
Pressure altitude is the altitude indicated with:
Altitude is the vertical distance measured from:
Altitude: desde el nivel del mar (QNH).
With QFE set, on the ground the altimeter reads:
With QNH set, on the ground the altimeter reads:
Which setting is associated with height above the aerodrome?
Only when taking off from sea level
QNH por debajo de la altitud de transición.
Atmospheric pressure at any point is caused by:
The weight of the air column above it
The temperature of the air there
The wind speed at that level
The humidity of the air only
Peso de la columna de aire.
Close to sea level in the ISA, pressure falls about 1 hPa every:
At 10 000 ft the pressure decrease is about 1 hPa per:
Más arriba cae más despacio: 36 ft.
Compared with standard, in cold air pressure decreases with height:
In warm air, the pressure at a given altitude compared with standard is:
Aire cálido: más presión en altura.
High air pressure at the aerodrome means:
Alta presión = baja altitud de presión.
Local QNH 1030 hPa, aerodrome elevation 2000 ft. Pressure altitude?
Local QNH 1002 hPa, aerodrome elevation 2000 ft. Pressure altitude?
Elevation 2000 ft, pressure altitude 2297 ft, OAT 27 °C. What is the density altitude?
ISA a 2000 ft = 11 °C → ISA +16 → +1882 ft → 4179 ft (ejemplo del temario).
Add 1000 ft to the pressure altitude
If the OAT is lower than ISA:
Height, altitude or flight level, as set
ISA: sea-level temperature and lapse rate are:
At 4000 ft the OAT is +17 °C. The ISA deviation is:
What is the ISA used for?
As a reference to compare real conditions
It is the actual atmosphere most days
It is a weather forecast model
With the QNH above 1013 hPa, the pressure altitude is ____ the elevation, and the performance is:
PA = elevación + (1013 − QNH) × 30. QNH > 1013 → PA menor → mejor performance.
The density altitude is obtained as:
DA = PA + 120 ft por cada °C de desviación sobre ISA.
The effect on the density altitude of temperature deviations compared with pressure deviations is about:
Pesan más los desvíos de temperatura que los de presión (≈ 4 veces).
If OAT is higher than ISA, the density altitude is ____ the pressure altitude and the performance is ____.
OAT > ISA → DA > PA → aire menos denso → peor performance. OAT < ISA → DA < PA.
To convert QFE into QNH you add:
About 1 hPa for every 30 ft of aerodrome elevation
About 1 hPa for every 300 ft of elevation
About 30 hPa for every 1000 ft of elevation
Nothing: QFE and QNH only differ in the units
ISA sea-level pressure can be expressed as ______ millibars.
ISA a nivel del mar: 1013,25 hPa = 1013,25 mb, 15 °C, 1225 g/m³.
ISA a nivel del mar: 15 °C y 1013,25 hPa.
The standard setting 1013.25 hPa is used:
Por encima del nivel de transición se vuela con 1013,25 hPa (niveles de vuelo).
021: The directive force of the Earth's magnetic field is its:
The angle of dip at that latitude
The angle between the total field T and its horizontal component H is the:
The aclinic line joins points where:
The angle of dip is zero
At the magnetic poles the directive force H is:
Moving from the magnetic equator towards a magnetic pole:
Más dip: menos H, más Z.
Above about 60° of latitude a magnetic compass is unreliable because:
The dip is large and H is small
The notional minimum horizontal field for a compass to work is about:
Two problems caused by the vertical component Z are:
Makes the needle dip and induces vertical magnetism, increasing deviation
Is the only force that aligns the compass with magnetic north
Increases the magnetic variation shown on the charts
Creates the agonic line where variation is zero
Inclina la aguja y aumenta la deviation.
The compass float's CG is displaced from the pivot in order to:
Corrige el dip (y crea turning/acceleration errors).
Acceleration errors of a direct-reading compass occur mainly on headings of:
NH, heading 270°, accelerating. The compass shows:
An apparent turn towards the north (e.g. 300°)
An apparent turn towards the south (e.g. 240°)
ANDS: acelerar → norte. Rumbo 270 hacia el N = números mayores.
NH, heading 090°, decelerating. The compass shows about:
At the magnetic equator, turning and acceleration errors are:
Turning errors of a direct-reading compass are zero when turning through:
Nulos en E y W, máximos en N y S.
In the northern hemisphere, when turning onto a southerly heading using the magnetic compass, you should roll out:
After the compass has passed the desired heading (overshoot)
Before the compass reaches the desired heading (undershoot)
Exactly when the compass shows the heading
NH, turning onto north: when the compass finally shows 360°, the aircraft has actually:
La brújula va por detrás: cuando marca 360 ya te has pasado.
In the southern hemisphere, accelerating on an easterly or westerly heading gives an apparent turn towards:
En el HS al revés: SAND (accelerate → south).
A line joining points of equal magnetic dip is:
Isoclinal = igual dip. Isogonal = igual variación.
Northern hemisphere: you turn left from 060°M onto north using the magnetic compass. When you are actually heading 360°M, the compass:
Still shows a heading short of north (about 020°), as if you had to keep turning
Already shows a heading past north (about 340°)
La brújula se retrasa al virar hacia el norte en el HN: aún marca ≈ 020. Hay que sacar el viraje antes (Undershoot North).
A direct-reading magnetic compass gives its most reliable indications:
Cerca del ecuador magnético: dip 0 y H máxima.
A direct-reading magnetic compass is designed to use:
The horizontal component of the Earth's magnetic field
The vertical component of the Earth's magnetic field
Usa la componente horizontal del campo magnético.
A direct-reading magnetic compass is most accurate:
Cerca del ecuador magnético la componente horizontal es máxima.
The compass will be most accurate:
Cerca del ecuador magnético el dip es pequeño y la componente horizontal es máxima: la brújula es más precisa.
The direct-reading magnetic compass becomes unreliable:
Cerca de los polos la componente horizontal es muy débil y la brújula pierde fiabilidad.
Turning through the north in the northern magnetic hemisphere, the compass will:
Indicate that you still have to keep turning when you have actually reached your desired heading
Indicate that you have passed your desired heading before you actually reach it
Turn continuously with no stopping it
UNOS: Undershoot North, Overshoot South. Girando por el norte la brújula se retrasa: parece que aún no has llegado cuando ya lo has hecho.
When turning through south in the northern hemisphere, the compass will:
Overshoot: indicate that you have passed the desired heading before reaching it
Undershoot: indicate that you have not yet reached it
Show a larger error than through north
Overshoot South: la brújula se adelanta, por lo que hay que salir del viraje antes.
What is the name of the angle between the horizon and the lines of magnetic force of the earth?
Dip (inclinación) = ángulo entre la horizontal y las líneas de fuerza. Variación = entre norte verdadero y magnético.
The angle between true north and magnetic north is called:
Variación (declinación magnética). Desviación = brújula vs. norte magnético.
